label: Computing the Camera Matrix P
notes: This chapter, printed pages 178 through 194, attacks camera resectioning: recovering the projection matrix from known three dimensional points and their measured images. We frame P as a geometric object with a center, a rank, and reprojection residuals, not merely a list of twelve numbers, and preview the DLT estimate that anchors the chapter.

label: The Resectioning Problem
notes: Resectioning assumes a calibration object with accurately known world coordinates imaged to noisy pixel measurements. Each correspondence is one equation source. The goal is the homogeneous three by four matrix mapping world points to image points, defined only up to scale, so eleven degrees of freedom must be pinned down from the data.

label: DLT Linear Equations
notes: The Direct Linear Transformation turns each correspondence into two independent rows by exploiting that the image point and its projection are parallel, so their cross product vanishes. Stacking these rows builds the design matrix A, and the camera vector p lives in its null space, recovered by singular value decomposition.

label: Minimal and Over-determined Solution
notes: Eleven unknowns need at least five and a half correspondences, so six points in general position give an exact minimal solution. More points over-determine the system; the singular vector for the smallest singular value gives the algebraic least squares answer, which we then must judge in pixels rather than trust blindly.

label: Data Normalization
notes: Raw pixel and world coordinates span wildly different magnitudes, wrecking the conditioning of A. We translate each cloud to its centroid and scale so the mean distance is root two in two dimensions and root three in three dimensions, run DLT on normalized data, then denormalize the matrix. This step is essential, not cosmetic.

label: Algebraic versus Geometric Error
notes: The DLT minimizes the algebraic residual A p, which has no direct geometric meaning. What we actually care about is the geometric image error: the pixel distance between each measured point and its reprojection. Inspecting residual vectors, not just the residual norm, reveals whether errors are random noise or structured model failure.

label: Gold Standard Refinement
notes: The gold standard estimate refines the DLT seed by minimizing total squared reprojection error over all eleven parameters using iterative nonlinear least squares such as Levenberg Marquardt. Under Gaussian image noise this is the maximum likelihood estimate, and the algebraic DLT solution merely provides the starting point for that descent.

label: Recovering K, R, t by RQ
notes: A finite projective camera factors as K times R bracket minus R C. Its leading three by three block is an upper triangular calibration matrix times a rotation, so an RQ decomposition splits it into intrinsics K and orientation R. The camera center C follows as the right null vector of P, fixing the translation.

label: Restricted Camera Estimation
notes: When skew is zero, pixels are square, or aspect ratio is known, the general projective camera over-parametrizes the problem. Restricted estimation fits only the free physical parameters, typically by minimizing geometric error with those constraints enforced. The result is less flexible but more honest, exposing wrong intrinsics that a full P would silently absorb.

label: Radial Distortion Correction
notes: Real lenses bend straight lines, displacing points radially from the principal point by an amount growing toward the periphery. Forcing a pinhole model onto distorted data leaves a structured, radially patterned residual field rather than random scatter. We fit or correct the distortion coefficients first, then judge the remaining residual as genuine measurement noise.

label: Calibration Lab Comparison
notes: The notebook fits three models on one synthetic two plane target: full projective DLT, a known intrinsics solvePnP pose, and a deliberately limited affine camera. DLT and solvePnP reach sub pixel error near zero point six seven pixels, while the affine model fails on perspective depth, its large residuals exposing the missing structure directly.

label: Recap and Checklist
notes: Resectioning turns correspondences into a homogeneous system solved by SVD, but every estimate must be validated geometrically. Normalize before DLT, inspect pixel residuals, factor P by RQ to read intrinsics and pose, restrict parameters when physics is known, and remove radial distortion before declaring the remaining error to be noise.
